Corporate & Business Law Practice Guide

Key Legal Considerations in Contract Drafting and Execution in Nepal

📅 Published: 2025-05-30
🔄 Updated: 2025-10-01
⏱ 7 min read
🔍 Review: Managing Associate Advocate, High Court Bar Association
Direct Legal Answer & Overview

Drafting an enforceable contract in Nepal requires strict alignment with the Muluki Civil Code 2074: 1) Ensuring both parties possess full legal capacity (18+ years, sound mind, corporate board authority); 2) Avoiding void agreement traps under Section 517 (restraint of trade, restraint of legal proceedings, impossible objects); 3) Formal signing and witnessing protocols under the Evidence Act 2031; and 4) Clear language defining governing law (Law of Nepal) and exclusive judicial or arbitral forum.

Key Practical Takeaways

  • Agreements containing complete restraints of trade are void under Section 517.
  • Corporate contracts must be backed by formal Board of Directors authorization.
  • Witness signatures on execution pages strengthen evidentiary presumption in court.

Copying a foreign contract template found on the internet and changing company names is a perilous commercial shortcut. A contract drafted for New York or London law often contains clauses that are strictly void under Nepalese public policy.

1. Void Agreement Traps under Section 517

Under Section 517 of the Muluki Civil Code 2074, certain covenants are void ab initio and unenforceable:

  • Restraint of Trade: A blanket clause preventing an employee or business from engaging in a lawful trade or profession is void, except for reasonable non-compete covenants upon the sale of company goodwill.
  • Restraint of Legal Proceedings: Any agreement prohibiting a party from approaching Nepalese courts or shortening statutory limitation periods is void.
  • Unlawful Consideration: Contracts founded upon transactions contrary to Nepalese law, public morals, or public policy are void.

2. Proper Execution & Witness Protocols

To ensure total evidentiary presumption under the Evidence Act 2031, commercial contracts in Nepal should be signed by authorized signatories on every page, stamped with the official company seal, and signed by at least two witnesses who provide their full names, addresses, and citizenship details.

Statutory Citations & Governing Nepal Legislation

Statute / Act Section / Rule Legal Significance
Muluki Civil Code 2074 Section 517 (Void Contracts) Enumerates contracts that are void ab initio under Nepalese law.
Evidence Act 2031 Section 23 (Attested Documents) Evidentiary weight of properly signed and witnessed commercial deeds.

Documentary Checklist for this Procedure

  • ✔ Executed signature and seal page with corporate board resolution
  • ✔ Signatures and citizenship copies of two witnesses

Frequently Asked Questions on this Topic

Can a contract in Nepal be written in the English language?

Yes. Commercial contracts between private parties can be executed in English. However, if litigation occurs in Nepalese courts, a certified Nepali translation prepared by a licensed legal translator must be submitted alongside the English original.
